Objective: The objective of the article is to identify and analyse the stages of the implementation of the principles making up the foundation for creating self-navigating organisations. Moreover, we analysed some areas of managing a company, related to the responsibility for decision-making processes in the strategic management of an organisation. We did it in the circumstances of a significant increase in staff participation in the company's activity. 
 Research Design & Methods: For the preparation of the case study, we used a qualitative method (participant observation, individual interview, partly categorized). Before initiating the proper research, we analysed the source information and data characterising the company and its activity, which were available both on the official websites of the company and also presented in the company information channels (company data, interviews with the members of the management, current information on the company activity). This allowed us to identify the company management method and the factors which generate the development of Sente SA. Further, this information has become the basis for the preparation of an interview questionnaire (see Appendix) which was intended to study the effect of the shared responsibility and participation principles applied in the company on the management of the company's strategic dimension in the context of an increase of the company's ability to self-navigate. 
 Findings: From the moment of the company's implementation of the management elements involving self-management and shared responsibility (including empowerment), financial results have significantly improved which was accompanied by an increase in a sense of responsibility for the company's objectives, achievements, and strategy among the company's staff. 
 Implications & Recommendations: The presented analysis of the process of implementing changes in the company's management and the stages of this process, as well as the identification of the limitations and challenges faced by the company management make up an important guideline for other researchers and practitioners in managing organisations who plan to further explore the problems described here or to change the manner of their company's operation and development by means of implementing teal management elements. Thanks to the practical example, performed analysis and the formulated guidelines, the challenges for the actions aiming at the increase of the potential of other organisations in the area of self-navigation and necessary changes in the process of strategic management, and the period necessary for an organisation to adapt to these changes will be shorter and more effective. 
 Contribution & Value Added: The article presents practical systematic principles and individual steps of implementing empowerment in the organisation and the stages of involving employees in the co-responsibility for the development of the organisation. (original abstract)

results.title: RGB
Chłopi południowej Małopolski wobec kryzysów żywnościowych od XVII do połowy XIX wieku

abstracts.content: The work concerns the identification and assessment of the impact of food crises, including their most severe form, that is, famine with catastrophic mortality, on the peasant community. The area under study is approximately 21,000 km2 located south of the Vistula River, constituting the southern part of historical Lesser Poland (Kraków and Sandomierz Voivodeships) until 1772, and after the occupation of these territories by Austria, six districts (circles) of western Galicia. | According to current knowledge, it is claimed that serious famines were not occurring in Poland until the 19th century. On the other hand, peasant economy throughout Europe dominated by so-called secondary serfdom was probably characterized by existence on the verge of subsistence, as feudal lords were claimed to limit the land cultivated by peasants to the necessary minimum, as well as their mobility and possibilities of other economic activities. The work covers two partially diverse periods: until the 1780s, when the lords had full power over their serfs, and after the reforms of Emperor Joseph II of Austria, when this power, as well as personal dependency, minor duties, and serfdom obligations were limited, and peasant land ownership became legally protected. | Peasants throughout the discussed period are formally divided (due to the nature of feudal obligations) into kmiecie (full tenants), zagrodnicy (smallholders), chałupnicy (cottagers), and komornicy (lodgers). Kmiecie owned the largest, self-sufficient agricultural farms and were obliged to perform serfdom with draft animals. The difference between zagrodnicy and chałupnicy mainly boiled down to the size of land owned because both groups provided forced labor services „on foot." Komornicy were theoretically a group without real estate, the most fluid, and one whose size was the most difficult to assess. | The first task was to determine the state of possession of the serfs. The areas of farms belonging to kmiecie at the end of the 18th century was highly diversified, from large ones, even over 20 hectares, mainly in lowland noble estates, to small ones, about five hectares, especially in mountainous areas. In the latter areas, regardless of the type of ownership (royal, ecclesiastical, noble), peasants did not perform services in the form of labor but paid for them in full or in part and freely inherited and divided farms. As a result, there were very few wealthy kmiecie-farmers in these areas. Generally, in the 18th century, there was an increase in the number of zagrodnicy (also due to the division of homesteads), and primarily chałupnicy and komornicy. Later, Austrian legislation made it difficult to divide farms, so until the first half of the 19th century, mainly the numbers of chałupnicy and komornicy were increasing in rural areas. | Old Polish measures of land area do not allow for precise determination of the sizes of former peasant farms. This was made possible only by the first Austrian land registry (so-called Josephine cadaster) from the 1780s. For 46 villages in foothill and lowland areas, the average size of a peasant farm ranged from about 2.5 to about 12 hectares. These data, as well as the average income from land calculated in money, allow for the calculation of the Gini coefficient showing the degree of wealth disparity among peasants. Based on data on the area or income from 85 villages, it was found that the Gini coefficient ranged from 0.24 to 0.73, indicating a high diversification within some villages, as well as differences even between neighboring villages. The most internally egalitarian were church villages, and the least internally egalitarian were those belonging to the poorest gentry owning single villages or only parts of them. In these circumstances, a large number of farms, even on fragmented kmiecie lands, were not self-sufficient in terms of food and had to buy grain for money earned from other agricultural activities, such as animal farming (e.g. sheep in the mountains), as well as non-agricultural activities such as fruit growing and trade, especially woodcraft and weaving (mainly linen), widely spread in all areas with poor conditions for crop cultivation. | The peasant diet was dominated by plant products, primarily rye, but with a strong correction for crops that were the easiest to access in a given area, especially oats in foothill and mountain regions. Already from the turn of the 18th and 19th centuries, potatoes dominated peasant tables, possibly reaching over 50% of the plant-based diet. | Grain production on peasant farms in most villages was insufficient for their inhabitants (per capita production), considering rye and barley. This situation depended not only on the structure of crops in a given region but also on the structure of land in the manor-serfs system. In the case of three villages (out of 170 surveyed), where the production of these two grains significantly exceeded local demand, there were no manorial farms. This indicates that manorial resources were the first potential food reserve, and their inclusion improved the situation of villages located in lowlands. The southern, foothill part of the region, where manorial farms were fewer or absent, relied on grain purchases from the north. Therefore, it is not surprising that the earliest mentions of widespread potato cultivation that date back to the 1760s and 1770s, originate from there. | The structure of peasant crops does not indicate that peasants were focused solely on meeting their own demand for food. On better soils, both kmiecie and zagrodnicy grew wheat, which they probably sold. Other crops also had a significant share: peas, millet, and buckwheat, which were sown late in spring, so they could to some extent replace inter-sown crops destroyed by winter. Another way to increase grain production on peasant farms was to limit fallow land. In many villages, on smaller farms, and even larger ones owned by kmiecie, all arable land was cultivated annually. Rational crop rotation methods were also used - already in the late 18th century, in some foothill villages, peasants practiced barley sowing after potato harvest on the same fields. | Previous research indicated slow demographic development of the region until the mid-18th century, mainly due to wars in the mid- 17th and early 18th centuries and due to waves of plague epidemics (the last one around 1710). However, it is certain that by the end of the 18th century, southern Lesser Poland (western Galicia) was the most densely populated part of the former Polish lands, with parishes exceeding 100 people per km2. | In order to examine the occurrence and scale of food crises and famines, information on extreme weather events since the late 16th century was analyzed, with an emphasis on the situation in the harvest months, partial data on fluctuations in grain yields (mainly data from manorial farms), and price movements of rye in Kraków and local prices. The main sources, especially for determining the intensity and effects of food crises, were parish registers of Roman Catholic parishes (75 parishes), primarily baptism records, to a lesser extent marriages and deaths (due to worse management and storage). It is known that only during food crises (especially famine) did the number of conceptions and births noticeably decrease. The synthesis of all the mentioned information allowed for the detection of several of the most serious crises in the pre-partition period: 1664/1665, 1676, 1714/1715, | and 1737. The last two were actually powerful famines with significant demographic consequences, resulting from at least two consecutive years of crop failure and confirmed in contemporary accounts. | In contrast to the famines mentioned above, the famine of 1847 was not entirely unknown. It was part of a pan-European crisis primarily caused by potato blight, but detailed information about it, even in the local press of that time, was very scarce. However, demographic data indicates that the population of western Galicia decreased by 9% in 1847, but this was just the beginning of an entire crisis decade, during which the population decreased by 17% by 1857. In the westernmost area of Galicia (Wadowice circle), population loss in some villages reached 25%. | The consequences of famines, beyond strictly demographic ones, including increased mortality, also as a result of dysentery and typhus in 1847, involved significant economic disruptions. 18th-century famines led to periodic abandonment of peasant farms or their indebtedness, collapse of grain exports to Gdańsk, labor shortages, and reduction in the number of working animals. Real assistance was provided exclusively by the manor, mainly in the form of loans in money or grain (at current high prices). However, it was different in 1847 when there was a visible erosion of the support system introduced after 1772. Faced with several years of crop failures and a bloody peasant revolt against the lords (1846), none of the significant institutions (state, manor, Church) provided adequate support to the peasants.

results.title: School Accessibility Assessment Questionnaire (KODS) – Presentation of the Tool and of Its Application

abstracts.content: Problem: The aim of the study was to develop and validate the School Accessibility Assessment Questionnaire (KODS) to assess the degree of accessibility of the school environment for students with disabilities and additional learning needs. Method: The tool consists of two parts: KODS-A to assess the accessibility of a school in general and KODS-B to assess accessibility for a specific student. A total of 462 Polish teachers and 1,302 parents took part in the survey, the former assessing the accessibility of schools for 3,838 students, and the latter – for 1,387 students. Results: The analyses confirmed the three-factor structure of the tool including architectural, didactic and socio-emotional accessibility. The KODS showed satisfactory psychometric properties, including reliability and validity. The results indicated significant differences in accessibility scores by type of school, educational stage and assessor. Conclusion: The KODS can serve as a tool for a comprehensive assessment of school accessibility and as a component of the School Functional Assessment of students.

The purpose of the paper is to examine the institution of arbitration characterized in the provisions of articles 1154-1217 of the Code of Civil Procedure, its advantages and to answer the question of whether arbitration is still an advantageous method of dispute resolution. The author draws attention to the most important advantages of arbitration. For a better understanding of the essence of arbitration, it was decided to quote excerpts from US court decisions, characterizing, among other things, the purpose of arbitration proceedings, as well as the arbitrator itself. The author points out that arbitration, although similar to litigation, is part of the alternative dispute resolution methods. The author presents arbitration as a process beneficial for parties.

Zwrócono uwagę na złożoność współwłasności łącznej, która wymaga zgody wszystkich współwłaścicieli na zarządzanie majątkiem, co zabezpiecza jego integralność do momentu zakończenia wspólności. Przeanalizowano również procedury podziału po ustaniu współwłasności oraz znaczenie wybranych umów majątkowych i orzeczeń sądowych, które wzbogacają praktyczny kontekst tematu. W artykule podkreśla się, że właściwe przygotowanie oraz zgodność z regulacjami prawnymi mają kluczowe znaczenie dla sukcesu inwestycji i ochrony interesów współwłaścicieli. (abstrakt oryginalny)

The article discusses key legal aspects related to the division of property, particularly in the context of joint co-ownership, marital assets, and the assets of civil partnership members. Various forms of division are presented, such as geodetic, legal, and land registry divisions, which allow procedures to be tailored to the specific needs of property owners. The complexity of joint co-ownership is highlighted, as it requires the consent of all co-owners for property management, ensuring the integrity of the assets until the co-ownership is dissolved. The article also examines division procedures following the termination of co-ownership, alongside the significance of marital agreements and selected court rulings, providing practical insights into the topic. In the article, it is emphasized that proper preparation and adherence to legal regulations are crucial for successful investments and the protection of co-owners' interests. (original abstract)

results.title: Water and its (un)conscious consumption: consumers and their water footprint in food products

abstracts.content: Water is a primary resource, essential for life on planet Earth. It is not only a beverage or an indispensable tool for human hygiene and personal care, but also, above all, an essential means for agriculture and livestock farming. The aim of this study is to verify, through a short survey among a sample of University students, studying in Italy, their knowledge of the concept of “water footprint”. In brief: are young consumers aware of the amount of water hidden within the food they regularly consume? To that end, a quantitative survey was conducted among young consumers at Italian Universities, using the “Computer-Assisted Web Interview” (CAWI) method. The results revealed a pronounced curiosity for this issue, counteracted by, unfortunately, a widespread unawareness of the water footprint of food products. The study focused on University students, who represent future consumers. For a more comprehensive research approach, the authors are already working on a new questionnaire to be administered in several European Union countries, aiming to involve a broader range of age groups. To the authors’ knowledge, this is the first quantitative study on young people studying in Italy referring  to their (un)conscious water consumption in relation to food choices.

results.title: Work-Life Balance in Poland Before and After the Implementation of Directive 2019/1158 : Could We Have Done More?

abstracts.content: The article aims to briefly highlight the historical background of the evolution of work-life balance regulations in Poland and outline recent legislative changes to the Labour Code in response to the implementation of Directive (EU) 2019/1158. This directive, in particular, seeks to improve employment conditions for women, who often spend significantly more time on unpaid caregiving responsibilities than on paid work, making it extremely challenging to balance work and family duties. Some of the new provisions, such as those concerning flexible working arrangements and the use of parental leave after maternity leave, should be assessed positively. However, there are drawbacks, including the relatively low maternity allowance for the non-transferable portion of parental leave, the unpaid nature of carers’ leave, and the setting of annual limits for carers’ leave, detaching this right from a specific case or person in need. Additionally, the lack of a clear definition of “force majeure” in relation to time off may create difficulties in applying the regulation and could potentially lead to abuses by both employees and employers. The authors attempt to assess the Directive’s impact on improving the reconciliation of professional and family life for employees, concluding that the Polish legislator could undoubtedly take further steps to ensure that working parents can more easily balance their professional and personal lives.

results.title: Recent Changes Regarding the Law Applicable to Maintenance Obligations in Ukraine

abstracts.content: The article concerns recent changes regarding the law applicable to maintenance obligations in Ukraine. The author analyzes the impact of the ratification of the 2007 Hague Protocol on the amendment of the Ukrainian Law on Private International Law of 2005. The accession to the 2007 Hague Protocol by Ukraine opens a new chapter in the scope of law applicable to maintenance in Ukraine. The law applicable to the maintenance obligation from parents in favour of children will no longer be determined by the connecting factor of citizenship but by the habitual residence. The habitual residence is the most appropriate connecting factor to determine the form and the amount of maintenance in a given situation. Determining the law applicable to the maintenance for children will be based on the correcting technique, designed to ensure that the creditor has the possibility of obtaining maintenance. In such a way the child’s interest is protected against the applicable law which does not guarantee such child the maintenance. Ukraine has joined the group of countries whose aim is to harmonize the governing laws applicable to the maintenance on a global scale because the 2007 Hague Protocol is the international agreement developed by the Hague Conference on Private International Law (HCCH).

abstracts.content: Purpose: The aim of this article is to provide an overview of the distortions in the comparability of economic and financial data that may occur in the course of economic analyses. Design/methodology/approach: The theoretical considerations presented in this publication are based on a critical analysis of the financial analysis literature. The problems presented are supported by numerous empirical examples (case studies). Findings: A properly prepared economic and financial analysis is most often based on a comparative analysis of the financial data under consideration. When conducting such an analysis, however, it should be taken into account that the data used in it may not be comparable. The ability to identify distortions (from different areas) may, nevertheless, allow correct conclusions to be drawn regarding the economic condition of the analysed economic entity. Originality/value: The originality of this publication results from the multi-faceted approach to the issue of economic analysis. The considerations combine aspects of accounting, finance or legal issues. In addition, both micro- and macroeconomic aspects are included in the course of the argument.

results.title: The multi-level governance and actors' perspective on technologies in migrants' integration

abstracts.content: This chapter investigates the impact of digital technologies in the integration of migrants, with a particular focus on the Ukrainian forced migrants who fled into Central and Eastern Europe (CEE). Unlike other migrant groups, Ukrainian forced migrants were, in many cases, warmly embraced by societies, with various players, including individuals, NGOs, and international actors, assisting or taking over responsibility from the state. This happens within the framework of complex and nuanced legislative and policy architecture related to integration as a whole, which varies across the region and states assumed to be the New Immigration Destinations (NID). The CEE approach to Ukrainian forced migrants exposes both unique and common characteristics, with the use of ICTs being one of the key features. Before delving deeper, the integration practices are examined and discussed, as they constitute the foundation for technologies. It is so as information and communication technology's (ICTs') role is significant as they help migrants navigate their new lives and organise assistance, from initial reception to settlement and integration. The authors, building on extensive qualitative research with experts, aid organisations, public sector and migrants, believe that such integration efforts would not have been possible without contemporary technological advancements and the supporting attitude of host societies.
